development_tools_and_models.notes: Claude Code (claude-sonnet-5) used interactively as the coding assistant for this entire exercise, in manual/non-auto mode (every diff reviewed before acceptance). No other coding assistant used.

plugins_and_extensions.notes: No IDE plugins or extensions beyond Claude Code itself.

application_models_and_parameters.notes: The application's own model integration (not the dev-time assistant): Anthropic Python SDK 2.8.0, model id 'claude-sonnet-5', max_tokens=1024, tool_choice default (model decides), system prompt in agent.py:SYSTEM_PROMPT. This SDK version's messages.create() does not expose a temperature/top_p parameter (checked via inspect.signature at build time) -- API default behavior used, not a conscious choice to omit it. Production hardening: (1) top-level cache_control=ephemeral on every call -- verified correct against this SDK's own docstring and covered by a test asserting the exact kwarg is sent, without needing a live API key; (2) transport-layer retry/backoff for 429/529, separate from the business-level MAX_SAVE_ATTEMPTS cap, with Retry-After read from the raw response header; (3) per-step usage/latency logged into each transcript, rolled up into a run-level cost/latency summary in run-report.json/.md (run.py:_aggregate_usage). Determinism layer added in a later pass: every tool's input schema is a Pydantic model (agent.py:TOOL_INPUT_MODELS) that is the single source of truth for both the JSON schema sent to Claude (generated via model_json_schema(), not hand-duplicated) and runtime validation of every tool_use the model sends -- a malformed call now degrades into a correctable, is_error-flagged tool_result instead of crashing the whole request with a bare KeyError/TypeError. is_error is set per Anthropic's documented tool-error convention, with an explicit distinction preserved between legitimate domain information (e.g. resolve_vendor's 'ambiguous: true', a real business-level save failure reported by the portal) and genuine tool-call errors (malformed input, controller vetoes). Model choice: claude-sonnet-5 kept over a cheaper model (e.g. Haiku) deliberately -- current published agentic-benchmark scores show a large quality gap (roughly 64 vs 24 on agentic tasks) for this specific workload (ambiguity detection, business-rule judgment), which is the actual point being assessed.

skills.notes: The starter pack's generate-assignment-data skill was read for guidance on extending seed data but not installed/invoked as a Claude Code skill -- its instructions were followed manually.

agent_instructions_and_subagents.notes: No Claude Code subagents or custom agent definitions were used to build this solution. (The solution ITSELF is an agent -- see application_models_and_parameters -- which is a separate thing from a Claude Code subagent.)

prompts_and_rules.notes: No global/user-level CLAUDE.md rules affected this exercise beyond default Claude Code behavior. The only exercise-specific prompt is the application's own SYSTEM_PROMPT in agent.py, which embeds the verbatim domain.md rules -- see that file.

permissions_and_environment_names.notes: Environment variable MODEL_API_KEY holds the Anthropic API key, supplied by the candidate (not provided by Provectus, per recruiter confirmation). Default Claude Code permission settings used, nothing project-specific configured.

testing.notes: 46 pytest tests, all runnable at zero API cost: tests/test_portal_client.py and tests/test_controller.py drive the real local portal via a real headless browser (free) to validate every controller invariant (ambiguity detection, field validation, retry cap, vendor-lock, controller-level duplicate veto, sanitization, recursive page-content sanitization) without calling Anthropic at all. tests/test_agent_loop.py uses a scripted fake Anthropic client (no network) to validate the tool-use loop's own control flow: that cache_control/system/tools are actually sent on every call, that MAX_STEPS exhaustion is reported honestly, and that the generated tool schema stays in sync with its Pydantic source models. tests/test_property_based.py adds a Hypothesis stateful-fuzzing test (RuleBasedStateMachine): it generates many random (including adversarial -- empty fields, unknown vendor_id, request_id collisions) sequences of controller tool calls against the real portal and asserts four hard invariants hold after every single step regardless of the sequence (retry cap never exceeded, no duplicate draft ids, no draft with a missing field, no draft against an unresolved vendor) -- a materially different and more rigorous technique than the hand-picked example tests, able to surface edge cases no one explicitly enumerated. This whole testing category isn't in the original template -- added because several of the production-hardening claims are only credible if something other than a live paid run verifies them. mypy was run once locally (not committed as config/CI, to avoid over-tooling a junior-scoped exercise) and the handful of genuine stale-annotation bugs it found were fixed; the remaining reported issues are an accepted, intentional trade-off of the dict-based tool-name dispatch pattern (mypy can't narrow a BaseModel subtype from a runtime string match) and were left as-is rather than restructured for marginal type-safety gain.
